body.statement: Can the lattice-residual handle prove a constant \(K_{\mathrm{res}}<\infty\), depending only on \((c,C,G)\), such that for every \(N\ge N_0\), on the scaled lattice \(E_{1,N}\), \[\sup_{p\in\mathcal P,\,|\gamma|\le G}\mathbb E_{\rho_{1,N}}\left|\{G_{1,N}-\mathcal L_{\gamma_N}\}h_{1,N}(X_{1,N})\right|\le K_{\mathrm{res}}N^{-1/2},\] including states whose upward or downward lattice jump crosses \(\gamma_N\)?
body.justification: This is the early-kill bound that converts the scaled mean approximation into the order \(N^{-1}\) effect-centering error required by fitted inference.
body.gap: Steady-state Stein results control static test functions, but no cited theorem gives this expected residual for the occupation Poisson solution at every ceiling phase and kink-crossing jump.
body.consumer: A positive answer validates diffusion-fitted inference for Keheala-like trials; failure leaves exact-center empirical inference as the defensible fallback.
